text: {"standards":[{"code":"L.6.3","verdict":"taught","reason":"The Literacy Lab 'Tense Check and Transition Phrases' has students underline verbs, fix tense shifts, and classify transitions in a model paragraph, applying language conventions to writing."},{"code":"L.6.3.b","verdict":"taught","reason":"The 'Formal or Casual?' turn-and-talk and the Model section's replacement of informal words with precise ones have students practice keeping style and tone consistent."},{"code":"W.6.2","verdict":"taught","reason":"In 'Draft and Strengthen the Essay,' students add relevant evidence from The Lightning Thief and a second source, explain it, and organize body paragraphs around their thesis."},{"code":"W.6.2.e","verdict":"taught","reason":"Students revise for formal style in the Model, Highlight Cohesive Devices, and Quick Write activities, replacing contractions, slang, and casual phrases."},{"code":"W.6.2.f","verdict":"taught","reason":"The Model discusses how a conclusion follows from the explanation, the Pulse Check tests this with a concluding-sentence item, and students draft their conclusions in the Draft step."}],"anchorText":{"verdict":"partly","reason":"The Lightning Thief is named in the Literacy Lab model sentences and drafting directions, but no specific passage or page from the novel is provided or read, and the Model relies on a teacher-written example essay."}}
